subject: An error when sliding surface semilandmarks

messages.author: 0115fa6682bc8072
messages.subject: An error when sliding surface semilandmarks
parts:
Dear all,

I am doing a pilot study about putting surface semilandmarks on a group of hominin and modern human skulls (14 hominin and 28 modern humans). The number of surface semilandmarks is 775, which is a lot. I acquired semilandmarks using the Landmark Editor and chose curve semilandmarks using the Geomorph package. 

I encountered a problem when I tried to test the intraobserver error as well as the influence of the scan quality. To test these factors, I re-generated semilandmarks from the scan of a specimen, which has been further repaired by the 'Meshdoc' function (for removing small holes and tunnels, etc.) in the Geomagic Studio 14. The regenerated semilandmarks acquired from the repaired scan should be nearly the same as the original semilandmarks. This is because after using the 'gpagen' function without sliding semilandmarks and running the 'plotRefToTarget' function, the thin-plate spline transformation shows nearly no transformation between grids of the original and the re-generated landmark sets. 

I then ran the 'gpagen' function with specifying surface and curve sliders. However, an error 'r in La.svd(X, k, k) : error code 1 from Lapack routine 'dgesdd' occurred when the process was 80% done. Interestingly, this error disappears after I replaced the regenerated semilandmark set with the original semilandmark set, though they should be nearly identical.

Does anybody have any idea about this error? I am not sure whether it has anything to do with the small sample size relative to the large number of semilandmarks, since previously the 'gpagen' function runs well with only 6 or 7 specimens. 

Thank you very much for taking time to look at my question!

Best regards,
Charles Zhang

messages.author: 4d71c6e24fb21497
messages.subject: RE: [geomorph-r-package] An error when sliding surface semilandmarks
parts:
Charles,

 

This error occurs because the SVD operation in Lapack fails to converge. (for context, Lapack contains the underlying set of Fortran code that R calls for many linear algebra operations, and is rather beyond the control of the R-package programmer).

 

There are many reasons why this issue could occur, and there are some interesting discussions related to the same error for other packages that use Lapack (e.g., vegan).  In your case, you mentioned that the issue only occurs with the regenerated dataset and not the original. Thus, the issue is in that second dataset.

 

Dean

 

Dr. Dean C. Adams
